title: Climate Change and Ecosystems
seo_title: Grade 9 Science (SNC1W): Climate Change and Ecosystems Worksheets (Ontario)
standard_text: Climate change indicators and the human contributions to climate change; the impacts of climate change on ecosystems and on communities in Canada, including First Nations, Métis and Inuit communities; and sustainable practices, including in agriculture. (summary of The Ontario Curriculum, Science, Grade 9: SNC1W (2022), Strand B: Sustainable Ecosystems and Climate Change)
meta_desc: Free Grade 9 Science (SNC1W) worksheets on climate change and ecosystems: the greenhouse effect, climate indicators, impacts on ecosystems and communities, carbon footprints and sustainable farming. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Extra greenhouse gases trap more heat and change ecosystems.
key_sub: Mitigation cuts emissions; adaptation copes with the changes.
body_html:
How to think about it

Greenhouse gases (carbon dioxide, methane, water vapour, nitrous oxide) absorb infrared energy given off by Earth's surface and keep the planet warm. Burning fossil fuels and clearing forests have raised the CO₂ level from about 280 ppm before 1800 to more than 420 ppm today, so more heat is trapped.

Indicators such as rising average temperatures, shrinking sea ice and glaciers, rising sea level and earlier spring melts show the climate is changing. Ecosystems respond: species shift their ranges, food webs change and some species cannot adapt fast enough. Sustainable practices such as cover crops, crop rotation and protecting wetlands store carbon.

Example

Why does melting Arctic sea ice speed up warming?

Ice reflects sunlight; dark ocean absorbs it.

Answer: the darker ocean absorbs more sunlight, a positive feedback

Example

Which gas has increased most because of burning fossil fuels?

Fuels contain carbon.

Answer: carbon dioxide

Common mistakes

  • Mixing up the greenhouse effect (natural and needed) with the enhanced greenhouse effect.
  • Thinking the ozone hole causes global warming.
  • Confusing weather (day to day) with climate (30-year averages).

items.q: How do wetlands help reduce the effects of climate change?

items.e: Peatlands and marshes hold large amounts of carbon in waterlogged soil.

items.q: Why does growing beans, peas or clover help the next crop?
c: they make the soil more acidic for good
bacteria in their roots fix nitrogen, which fertilizes the soil

items.e: Legumes reduce the need for synthetic fertilizer.

items.q: What is a climate change indicator?
c: a measurement that shows how the climate is changing, such as sea-ice extent or average temperature
items.e: Indicators are tracked over many years to show trends.

items.q: Which change reduces greenhouse gas emissions from transportation?
c: idling the car to keep it warm
taking transit, cycling or using electric vehicles charged from clean electricity
items.e: Most transport emissions come from burning gasoline and diesel.

items.q: Which is an example of adapting to climate change rather than slowing it?
c: switching from coal to wind power
building higher flood walls and planting trees for shade in cities
items.e: Mitigation reduces the cause; adaptation reduces the damage.

items.q: What is a carbon sink?
c: something that takes in more carbon dioxide than it releases, such as a forest or the ocean
items.e: Oceans, soils and forests remove CO₂ from the atmosphere.

items.q: Which technology is designed to reduce this impact: fertilizer runoff causing dead zones?

items.e: Engineers design solutions that reduce harm to natural systems.
